trace.code: zstd_do_write() calls ZSTD_decompressStream() and only checks ZSTD_isError(); it ignores the 'remaining' hint, so a truncated frame is accepted.

zstd_encoding registers Curl_cwriter_def_flush (no incomplete-stream check), while deflate_do_flush/gzip_do_flush/brotli_do_flush all added the 'stream ended before completion' check (commits 0036b55, f789f35).

preconditions: curl built with zstd support (libzstd) and --compressed / HTTP content decoding enabled (the default)
a server (or MITM) serves a truncated Content-Encoding: zstd response body

evidence.observed_result: Real curl built with zstd+zlib (zig cc): a truncated Content-Encoding: gzip body -> 'curl: (61) Gzip stream ended before completion' (REJECTED). The same truncated Content-Encoding: zstd body -> exit 0 and 1996 bytes of decompressed data written (ACCEPTED). zstd_encoding uses Curl_cwriter_def_flush, so the incomplete-stream hardening added to gzip/deflate/brotli (0036b55/f789f35) is missing for zstd.
